chapter: Early recordings and arrival in New York
title: Listening to 'Stop, You're Breaking My Heart' and the session musicians
summary: They play the 14 June 1937 side and Maxine names the studio players she remembers, including Manny Klein, Artie Bernstein and Chauncey Morehouse.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I see. Okay, would you like to play 'Stop, You're Breaking My Heart?' And maybe we can --
I don't have 'Stop, You're Breaking My Heart.'
I have it on my tape here.
You got it? I'd love to hear it.
I don't think we mentioned that that was the 14th of June 1937 -- the date of that session was. You have any recollection about any of the musicians with you?
Well as I said before, I was so new in the city, I hadn't even had a chance to be introduced to all of the musicians that were around. But looking at this line-up here, we had
some pretty heavies here. Like Manny Klein, Charlie Spivack, Jack Lacey, Toots Mondello, Jess Carneol, Babe Russin. Babe Russin had made some records with me later. I knew him.
Eddie Powell, Claude Thornhill, of course. I thought when I heard this record a few months ago, 'Stop, You're Breaking My Heart,' I didn't know that that was Claude.
But -- on vibes -- but I don't think that's vibes. I think that's more marimba because it had that wooden sound.
Artie Bernstein, bass -- I worked with him later. Chauncey Morehouse, Jimmy Farrell -- I didn't even know who the other vocalist was on that date.

Because I never heard 'Stop, You're Breaking My Heart' as a release. And when my son played it for me a couple of months ago, I listened. And all of a sudden, it dawned on me that it was my recording that I had made forty-something years
